methodological_rigor.justification: The study introduces and tests GENEVA across pooled 3D cultures, organoids, CDX/PDX xenografts, single-cell profiling, drug-combination assays, and in vivo CRISPRi screens, providing orthogonal validation of KRAS-G12C inhibitor response mechanisms. Methods are detailed for pooling, demultiplexing, sequencing, xenografts, compound dosing, quality control, differential expression, enrichment, synergy modeling, and guide scoring. Limitations include no statistical sample-size predetermination for in vivo experiments, small animal group sizes for some validation studies, no blinding of data collection or analysis, and some assays with only one or two biological replicates. Statistical methods are generally appropriate but heterogeneous, with normality assumed but not formally tested and limited correction detail outside selected analyses such as Benjamini-Hochberg for guide scoring.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is preclinical mechanistic and platform-development work using cell lines, organoids, xenografts, and CRISPRi screens, so it maps to Oxford level 5. Its translational relevance is substantial because KRAS-G12C inhibitors are clinically used and the study identifies mitochondrial activity and EMT-related pathways as candidate determinants of response and combination strategies. The clinical path remains indirect because no patient treatment cohort tests the predicted combinations or biomarkers.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE is applicable for the animal components, while the manuscript also reports extensive single-cell and experimental methods. It provides animal strain, age, housing, maximum tumor size, implantation, dosing, random allocation of mice, exclusion criteria, replicate counts, sequencing and computational pipelines, and source data for figures. Reporting gaps include no in vivo sample-size calculation, no blinding, and limited detail on allocation concealment. Source data are provided and methods are reproducible, but open analysis code or a full computational workflow repository is not clearly stated in the manuscript.

novelty_literature.justification: The GENEVA platform is a strong methodological contribution because it multiplexes genetically diverse tumor models within pooled 3D and in vivo systems while preserving single-cell resolution and endogenous controls. The biological application to KRAS-G12C inhibitors extends prior work on resistance and combination therapies by linking pooled response heterogeneity to mitochondrial respiratory activity, EMT, mTOR, TGF-beta, and in vivo CRISPRi validation. Prior single-cell perturbation and KRAS resistance literature exists, but the integrated mosaic in vivo platform and its drug-response use case are highly original.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized around platform validation, in vivo extension, mechanistic discovery, combination testing, and CRISPRi screening. The abstract and introduction clearly explain the scalability problem in preclinical models and the rationale for KRAS-G12C inhibitor testing. Figure captions are detailed and provide sample sizes, treatment conditions, statistical tests, and interpretation aids for complex single-cell plots. The density of methods and multi-panel results is high, so some sections are demanding to read, but the core narrative remains coherent.

key_strengths: Novel GENEVA platform integrates pooled genetically diverse tumor models with single-cell readouts in vitro, in organoids, and in xenografts.
Orthogonal validation spans drug-response profiling, Seahorse and flow assays, in vivo combinations, and CRISPRi screens.
Clinically relevant KRAS-G12C inhibitor biology is connected to mitochondrial activity, EMT, and candidate combination strategies.
Methods and figure captions provide extensive technical detail and source data for complex single-cell and animal experiments.
key_concerns: No statistical methods were used to predetermine in vivo sample sizes, and some validation experiments have small replicate counts.
Data collection and analysis were not blinded to experimental conditions.
Several translational claims remain preclinical and require validation in patient-derived clinical cohorts or treatment studies.
The breadth and complexity of assays may make it hard to distinguish platform performance from biology specific to selected models.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a high-novelty preclinical platform and mechanistic study with broad translational relevance to KRAS-targeted therapy. Tier 1 with minor revisions is plausible, mainly requiring tighter framing of preclinical limitations and statistical rigor.
